reproduced_predecessor.scope: Exact reviewed current vendored adapter on synthetic HTTP objects; no provider or production packet reads.

repairs: The auction-local FRED wrapper reads at most two MiB plus one byte from the original response and closes it. Exact response URL, HTTP 200, declared whole-body length, plain encoding and finite duplicate-free observation JSON are checked before caching.
Normal file read/close semantics replace the old wrapper that ignored requested byte limits. Every cache reader has its own cursor and metadata copy.

Warm hits preserve original request/acquisition times, sanitized source identity and exact body hash/length. Cache lookup after clock rollback refreshes; import remains idempotent; unrelated hosts/endpoints pass through.

The original four-attempt transient retry policy and thirty-minute cache remain. Failed refresh cannot return an expired body. Nonretryable/protocol failures do not issue extra retries, and diagnostics cannot serialize credential-bearing exception text.

The native cross-source adapter binds the optional transport record to exact response bytes, public query identity, clocks and cache age. Read time remains distinct from acquisition time; safe failure reasons remain visible without original-source qualification.
A reproduced difference in Windows time.time versus datetime.now precision could falsely classify acquisition as future. Adapter and consumer now use one clock conversion, covered by a regression.
browser_scope: No page or renderer changes. Stage 405 isolated responsive/recovery acceptance is preserved; the complete frontend suite is rerun.
limitations: Acquisition metadata is recorded by this reviewed adapter, not independently signed provider publication evidence. Immutable FRED original retention and exact whole-model replay remain unimplemented.
Historical first-release availability, underlying provider definitions, cache population capacity and native peak-resource measurements remain unverified.

Other Lambdas and the fleet-wide shared shim are unchanged. The remaining auction DFF/benchmark acquisition, legacy caches, analog/history/issuance calculations and predictive qualification still need separate review.
No Calls, sizing or execution authority follows from transport completeness. Ordinary publication remains separate from deployment acceptance.
